## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` doesn't lower-case keys, but `get` does, so any key containing an uppercase letter is stored and can never be read back. This must be fixed before merge. The new round-trip test misses this because it only calls `set` with a lowercase key.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` writes `self._store[key]` with the key unchanged, while `get` (app/cache.py:17) looks up `key.lower()`. As a result, `c.set("Alpha", 1); c.get("Alpha")` returns `None`, and the `"Alpha"` entry stays in `_store` forever because `get`'s expiry cleanup only deletes the lower-cased key. This breaks the rule stated at app/cache.py:14-15: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together". Could you store under `key.lower()` in `set`, and add a test that calls `set` with a mixed-case key? — Callers using mixed-case keys silently get cache misses every time, and their entries pile up in memory with no expiry.

## Strengths
- `test_entries_expire` (tests/test_cache.py:21-27) uses a monkeypatched `time.monotonic` clock to test expiry. Both `set` and `get` read `time.monotonic` through the module attribute, so the patch reaches them and the test can't flake on timing.
